reuse.why: The shared getScheduleAmount now serves the template, forecast, preview, post and action-sync paths (schedule-template's own midpoint copy was routed through it), but the API's expectedAmount re-implements the rule inline and the approximate tolerance re-implements getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: scheduleModel.toExternal keeps its own range rule (furthest from zero) beside getScheduleAmount, and getScheduleAmount repeats the Math.round(Math.abs(x) * 0.075) tolerance that getApproxNumberThreshold already defines.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts where the tree keeps schedule-amount logic, but the API model layer computes its own amount instead of delegating.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule, the API field and the needed type tweaks, though several comments edited along the way are left wrong.

maintainability.why: After step 4 the API's expectedAmount silently disagrees with the helper (furthest from zero, ignores isapprox), and comments still say 'furthest from zero', so a maintainer has two rules to keep in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: scheduleModel.toExternal in packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts computes expectedAmount itself instead of calling getScheduleAmount(schedule._amount, schedule._amountOp); getScheduleAmount's isapprox branch bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts expresses the range rule as an abs-comparison ternary rather than Math.min/getScheduleAmount, and the tolerance in getScheduleAmount is an inline formula rather than a call to getApproxNumberThreshold.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleAmount (shared/schedules.ts) gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; scheduleModel.toExternal (server/api-models.ts) re-implements the amount instead of calling it.
